chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Abu Usamah who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the garment in which there is major ritual impurity (janabah), and the rain falls upon me until it drenches me. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem.'

key_terms.الْجَنَابَةُ: Major ritual impurity requiring full body wash

ai.seo_question: Does rain purify a person in janabah?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that rainwater acts as a purifying agent for the body and clothes of one in *janabah*, thereby satisfying the requirement for ritual purity without necessitating an immediate, separate *ghusl*. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that natural water sources are inherently pure (*mutlaq*) and effective for removing major impurity, provided the water reaches the skin or garments. It underscores the practical ease (*rukhas*) granted in ritual purification when natural elements interact with the state of impurity.
